origin.title: How ZED TECH was born
origin.paragraph1:
I develop a new feature for an e-commerce site.
Result: almost no impact on sales.
origin.paragraph2:
By analyzing the data, the real problem appears:
massive cart abandonment at checkout.
origin.paragraph3:
I try to customize the payment flow.
Wall. Technical limitations everywhere.
origin.paragraph5: If the problem is at checkout, why doesn't anyone really solve it?
origin.paragraph6: 8 years later, 10,950 hours of R&D, 47 migrations: the answer is here.

mission.h2: Bringing human warmth back to e-commerce
mission.manifesto:
Bringing human warmth back to e-commerce

ZedTech is not another lab promising to 'disrupt' e-commerce with smarter algorithms.

I am an independent researcher-developer wondering:

What if I used tech—including AI—to rehumanize the experience?
What if conversations replaced forms?
What if catalogs became living showcases again?
What if automation served warmth rather than coldness?

My research doesn't seek to 'scale' or 'optimize'.
It seeks to restore life. Warmth. Emotion.

Because your customers are not conversion rates.
They are humans who deserve a real experience.

phase1.title: The wrong problem
phase1.description: I built a search engine so customers could book according to THEIR availability.
phase1.result: Result: Almost no impact on conversions.

phase2.title: Digging deeper
phase2.description: I simulated the complete customer journey. Discovery: Too many steps. Too much information. Too much friction. I shortened. Simplified. Optimized.
phase2.result: Result: +2% conversions. A slight improvement, but nothing satisfying enough.
phase2.product: I was still looking in the wrong place.

phase3.title: The epiphany
phase3.description: The problem wasn't the journey. It was the final step: checkout. Cold form. 15 fields. 0 human reassurance.
phase3.context: Classic e-commerce platforms limit customization of this critical step.
phase3.result: Finally, I saw where the real friction was.
phase3.product: Checkout was killing conversions. Not the journey.

phase4.title: The solution
phase4.description: What if checkout was no longer a form, but a conversation?
phase4.product: We now know how to do it. We're figuring out how to make it available to others.

phase5.title: Stabilize and distribute
phase5.description: All of 2025: R&D, iterations, monitoring. Make the solution stable and accessible.
phase5.context: Simplified onboarding, responsive support, clear documentation

lesson.line1: 80% of the work: reinventing the journey.
lesson.line2: 20% of the work: optimizing checkout. +23% conversions.
